decisive_items: She had been diagnosed with a tenosynovial giant cell tumor by MRI at a local hospital
Post-contrast images demonstrated homogeneous enhancement of the tendons and synovial membrane, supporting synovial hyperplasia
a neoplastic lesion remained in the differential
response.rationale: The prior MRI diagnosis of tenosynovial giant cell tumor, progressive localized hand/wrist symptoms, and imaging showing an enhancing synovial/tendon lesion with restricted diffusion and secondary median nerve compression make TGCT the most likely unifying diagnosis; the other candidates are descriptive findings or preliminary differential entries rather than the primary neoplastic process.

rejected.why: Tenosynovitis is a component of the imaging findings but does not account for the prior TGCT diagnosis or restricted diffusion neoplastic lesion.
Only minor carpal bone degenerative changes are present; this does not explain the soft-tissue/synovial enhancement or median nerve compression.
Synovial hyperplasia is seen in TGCT and is not a separate primary diagnosis.
Median nerve compression is secondary to the synovial/tendon lesion, not the primary etiology.
Same entity as R1 under an alternative name; R1 matches the exact terminology used in the vignette.
